issues.legal_issue: A court should take a justice-oriented and lenient approach to condonation of delay in a public authority’s appeal when deliberate lapses by public officials caused the delay and corrective steps were taken after the proceedings came to light.
material_facts: A town panchayat sought condonation of a 1373-day delay in filing a second appeal.
The Executive Officer took no steps at the relevant time, and the Supreme Court found that the delay was caused by deliberate lapses on the part of the officer then in charge.

The later Executive Officer learned of the proceedings when eviction steps were taken in execution, then sought certified copies and filed the appeal after obtaining sanction and completing procedural formalities.
The High Court had refused to condone the delay.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the refusal, condoned the delay, and remitted the matter to the High Court for consideration of the second appeal in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Under State of Nagaland v. Lipok Ao and others, (2005) 3 SCC 752, a court considering condonation of delay must adopt a justice-oriented approach. Where it is convinced that government officials or public servants attempted to defeat justice by causing delay, it should, in the larger public interest, take a lenient view, condone the delay however large, and allow the matter to be decided on its merits.

predicates.public_authority_appeal_delay_applicatio: A public authority sought condonation of delay in filing an appeal.
predicates.deliberate_official_lapses_caused_delay: Deliberate lapses by public officials caused the delay in taking the appeal forward.
predicates.corrective_steps_followed_discovery: After a responsible official learned of the proceedings, steps were taken to obtain the necessary documents and file the appeal.

issues.definition: When a public authority seeks condonation of appeal delay, deliberate official lapses caused that delay, and corrective steps follow discovery, the delay is condoned.
